name: Off-Road Vehicle
description: A motorized vehicle not designed for highway use and capable of cross-country travel over natural terrain, such as an electric dirt bike. Alabama sets no power or speed limit for it and has no off-highway sticker for two-wheelers. Off-road vehicles of model year 2026 or later must be titled, though the title law names only ATVs and side-by-sides.

restrictions.rule: Not designed for highway use and capable of cross-country travel over land, snow, ice, marsh or other natural terrain
No limit on motor power or speed

For title, an off-road vehicle is one not built to federal motor vehicle safety standards, which the law says includes ATVs and side-by-sides without naming two-wheelers; since January 1, 2026 one of model year 2026 or later must be titled, and none more than 10 model years old is titled

Alabama's voluntary three-year registration sticker covers only all-terrain vehicles (three or more non-highway tires) and recreational off-highway vehicles (four or more), not a two-wheeled off-road motorcycle
Alabama law sets no statewide minimum age, helmet or safety-course rule for riding one off the highway
Since October 1, 2025, can't be ridden in a creek, stream or other waterway, or on land under navigable or non-navigable waters, except on land the rider owns or has permission to use
Barred from the Gulf of Mexico beaches and sand dunes off public roads, parking places and private driveways
On a public road a two-wheeled one is held to the motorcycle rules: a license tag, a Class M license and a helmet
